rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every referent resolves within-file: 'this training', 'the rules and checks', 'the result', 'Claude'. 'The rules file you just wrote' (chunk 2) and 'the bug today' (chunk 3) are session artifacts from the exercises the student just ran (compound-and-close writes ./CLAUDE.local.md, described in curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md as 'a rules file written from session evidence'; the prework bug is consumed by fix-tests-first per getting-going.md's wiring table) — carve-out applies.
No positional cross-file callback. Klaassen is named directly with his claim unpacked in the same sentence ('Kieran Klaassen calls this compound engineering: work produces evidence...').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'The rules file you just wrote' verified against curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md, which precedes this lecture in getting-going.md's Start here order and produces exactly that artifact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal structure present in this lecture.
Chunk 0 is a standard title/lede slide; chunks 1-3 each carry multiple self-carrying claims, none is a bare wait-state.

Each header matches its chunk's content under the sequential read: chunk 1 opens on the bulletpoint origin and rule-correction story; chunk 2's testing-layer content matches 'Then we tested the training'; chunk 3's loop-naming and CLAUDE.local.md content matches 'You just ran the same loop'.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triple ('Some were too broad. Some fired in the wrong place.' is a pair, under the cap); no self-grading superlative; the rule/commit count carries an interpretive caveat ('Neither count is a claim that more rules make better work'), not a self-retraction of the number's accuracy, so it does not trip the number+retraction shape; no abstraction-noun stack (bulletpoints, checklists, commits, judges, simulations, tmux runner all stay concrete); no empty-leg verb triplet.
